title: EventStream resume tokens, partial-object framing, and function-call streaming compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Clients need reliable resume behavior, deterministic partial-object framing for structured outputs, and a compatibility shim for older clients that expect chunked HTTP transfers. We also need streaming support when the model emits function-call tokens mid-stream (so downstream tools receive stable, parseable messages).

Goal: Deliver an EventStream-based streaming protocol variant that includes lightweight resume tokens, a partial-object framing convention for safely emitting incremental JSON-like structured outputs, and a compatibility layer that maps EventStream to chunked-transfer semantics for legacy SDKs. Ensure function-call emissions can be reassembled deterministically across reconnects without duplicating side effects.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can reconnect after a network interruption and resume mid-response using a concise resume token: server provides token at regular safe-program points and client can request resume starting from token.

Partial-object framing is defined: each event has stable metadata (event-type, seq, resume_token_optional) and payloads are incremental JSON deltas that can be merged to produce the final structured output without ambiguity.

Function-call streaming: function call start / argument chunks / function-call-complete events are defined and are idempotent on resume — server must provide call-id and replay logic to avoid delivering duplicate call intents to downstream tool relays.

Compatibility shim converts EventStream events to HTTP chunked transfers for legacy SDKs without changing semantic guarantees (ordering, resume semantics via chunk-aligned tokens), documented and tested.
Automated tests: unit + integration tests for reconnect/resume across server and two different client implementations (node-python).
Benchmarks: resume token size and overhead measured; added latency <3ms p50 for streaming hot path on internal perf harness.
tasks: Design resume token format and placement in event stream
Define partial-object framing and example schemas for structured outputs
Function-call streaming protocol spec (call-id, start, args-chunk, end, replay rules)
Implement server-side resume token emission points and in-memory checkpointing
Implement compatibility shim module that exposes chunked-transfer endpoint mapping to EventStream
Add unit/integration tests and client test harness (node + python) for reconnect + resume
Performance run and telemetry instrumentation for resume token overhead
comments: 2025-02-13 - Aisha: Kickoff notes uploaded to Confluence (link below). Decided to avoid embedding full KV cache offsets in token; token will be a compact opaque reference mapped to server checkpoint state.

2025-02-18 - Liam: Prototype complete for resume tokens (server stores ephemeral checkpoint in redis with 1h TTL). Basic resume works for short responses; need to handle long-lived streams and tombstoning.

2025-02-21 - Design review (Mariana Ruiz): Suggested adding explicit backpressure hint in events to avoid client-side busy loops when reconnecting rapidly. Agreed, added 'backpressure_hint' optional field.

2025-02-25 - Eng review: Implemented function-call call-id and chunking. Found race where reconnect could replay the last argument chunk; resolved by making finalization idempotent and introducing 'call-seq' monotonic counter.

2025-02-27 - QA: Integration tests with node-sdk show compatibility shim successfully maps EventStream frames to chunked-transfer lines. Found one parsing edge-case with CRLF in payloads; fixed by base64-encoding binary sections.
